test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What key principle did the Supreme Court emphasise in the 2024 Property Owners Association v State of Maharashtra case?

options.text: Only scarce or vital resources justify state takeover
Public trust doctrine applies to all private assets.
State can acquire all private properties at will.
Government power overrides individual property rights.

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only scarce or vital resources justify state takeover**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court highlighted that the principle of state takeover applies only to **resources that are scarce or vital** for public interest.
 
• This decision reinforces the idea that state intervention in private property must be **well-justified** and limited to cases where it is necessary for **public welfare**.
 
• The judgment is significant as it places a **limit on the state's authority** over private property, safeguarding **individual rights**.
 
• It aligns with the constitutional provisions in India, particularly **Article 300A**, which ensures that private property can only be acquired under the authority of law.
 
• By emphasizing this principle, the Supreme Court aims to prevent misuse of power and protect the rights of **property owners**.
 
• It also reflects the judiciary's commitment to upholding the **rule of law** in cases related to property rights and acquisition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Public trust doctrine applies to all private assets**__

 __
 
• This doctrine suggests that certain resources are preserved for public use and the government must protect and maintain them. However, it does not apply to **all private assets**, but to resources like **water bodies, forests, and other natural assets**.
 
• In the context of the case, the application of this doctrine to all private assets would have been deemed **overarching and unjustified**.
 
 
 
• **State can acquire all private properties at will**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because it contradicts the Indian Constitution's principles, particularly **Article 300A**, which ensures that private property can only be acquired by the state under legal authority.
 
• Such unrestricted acquisition would lead to potential misuse of power and infringe upon **individual rights**.
 
 
 
• **Government power overrides individual property rights**__
 
 
• This option undermines the balance between government authority and private rights as established in the Constitution of India.
 
• While the government has the right to acquire property for public purposes, it must adhere to **legal procedures** and ensure fair compensation.
